title: Persona Mini-Packs (brainpad): curated micro-personas for private/edge inference
content:
Quick sketch: bundle tiny persona artifacts (LoRA adapters, instruction templates, shallow metadata) as "mini-packs" that operators can deploy with Redwood Private or Dedicated pools. Goal is fast personalization for customers who want per-customer or per-team personas without a full fine-tune lifecycle and with tight resource constraints (edge or limited GPUs).

Why:
- Customers want consistent brand/voice/guardrails per tenant but cannot afford heavy model forks.
- On-prem and VPC cases especially benefit from small binary artifacts that sit next to a base model (lower compliance surface).
- Enables product story: "install a persona pack, route traffic, measure quality" rather than "train a new model".

Core idea:
- A Persona Mini-Pack = small adapter + prompt manifest + prefetched KV snippets + quick eval set for regression checks.
- Adapter format: LoRA/adapter weights (quantized), or delta-prompts (if too constrained), plus a small metadata json describing personality/guardrails/whitelist tokens.
- Manifest: sample prompts, negative examples, pre/post-processing hooks (simple rules).
- Eval harness: 10–50 curated cases the pack owner provides; Redwood runs lightweight checks on deployment for regressions.

User stories / acceptance criteria:
- As a platform admin, I can upload a pack (zip) and see quick validation (size, missing fields, unsafe tokens).
- As a product manager, I can pin a persona pack to a route; users hitting that route get persona behavior with <50ms extra latency.
- As an SRE, I can deploy packs to Dedicated pools and see per-pack metrics (usage, error, drift) in Console.
- As a security officer, I can set that packs are allowed only in Private/VPC, not in hosted multi-tenant usage.

Technical considerations / constraints:
- Format: establish a tiny standardized manifest spec (v1) so adapters are portable between deployments. Keep strictly flat: name, version, base-model-compat, adapter-file, prompt-presets, eval-cases.txt, size-bytes, signed-manifest(optional).
- Storage: store packs in object store with signed metadata; avoid storing full weights in control-plane for Private deployments if customers require it.
- Inference path: on model load, runtime checks base-model compatibility > applies LoRA/adapters into memory space (prefer runtime composition if supported) > if not, fallback to prefixing prompts with condensed instruction template.
- Latency target: additional token latency budget <= 20ms for in-memory adapter application; if on-demand patching needed, warm caches or preapply at model startup.
- Memory & GPU: adapters must be quantized to small size (<=50MB target) for edge; recommend quantization profiles and shipping with a compressor tool.
- Safety/regulatory: packs must be scanned (automated heuristics) for instructions that try to override safety system; packs flagged require manual review.

Rollout & operations:
- Phase 0: internal hackathon build to prove flow in Dedicated testpool (one team).
- Phase 1: private customers opt-in (beta) with console UI to upload and pin packs. Collect telemetry: per-pack requests, latency, quality delta vs baseline.
- Phase 2: add marketplace-style catalog for vetted community packs (requires legal/terms).
- Monitoring: attach pack-level evals; fail deployment if regression > threshold; offer automatic fallback to base-model route.
- Billing: optional add-on charge per pack deployment + storage + per-token delta if pack induces higher compute. Need to coordinate pricing with biz ops.

Open questions / risks:
- How do we represent multi-adapter stacks? (stack order, composition semantics).
- Base-model compatibility matrix maintenance. Could be heavy as models update. Need per-pack compatibility tag + automatic compatibility check against runtime kernels.
- Security risk: packs as attack vector (prompt injection, covert instructions). Require mandatory static analysis + runtime policy enforcement.
- Intellectual property: who owns the adapter weights? licensing model for community packs.
- Evaluation: small eval sets may overfit; need conservative rollouts and A/B tests.

Prototype tasks (next actions):
- [ ] Define v1 manifest spec (1 pager) + sample zip layout. Owner: Micah.
- [ ] Quick CLI: pack create/check (compress + generate manifest + scan). Owner: Drew.
- [ ] Runtime: minimal support to load/apply LoRA inflater at model-init in Dedicated devpool. SRE pairing. Owner: Keisha.
- [ ] Console: small upload UI + pin-to-route control. Owner: Product UI.
- [ ] Safety: simple blacklist/regex scan prototype and hook into existing policy engine. Owner: Sana.

Notes / heuristics to keep it pragmatic:
- Start with only two adapter backends: LoRA (preferred) and prompt-prefix templates (fallback). Keep the first explorer conservative.
- Limit pack size and require a manifest-version. Avoid arbitrary binaries in the first iteration.
- Avoid marketplace until we have safety + licensing sorted. Beta only internal & opt-in customers.

Example manifest (informal):
name: "acme-support-voice-v1"
version: "1.0.0"
author: "acme-corp"
base_model: "redwood/llama-2-13b"
adapter: "adapters/acme-support-lora.pt.q4"
prompt_presets: ["support-short","support-diagnostic" ]
eval_cases: "evals/001.txt"
size_bytes: 34872340
compatibility: ["llama-2-13b-causal","llama-2-13b-causal-q4"]

Open TODOs for review meeting:
- Cost model brainstorm (storage vs runtime vs per-token uplift).
- Decide whether to allow third-party packs in hosted product (likely NO for now).
- Define minimal safety rules for automatic rejection.

If anyone reading: add quick thoughts inline; I expect lots of missing edgecases. This doc intentionally rough — want to use it to prep a short pitch for the product council (10 min).

-- Micah
